prompt: Help me set up a standard AMM style smart contract with move.  It should support: creating a liquidity pool for two coin types, adding and removing liquidity (minting/burning LP tokens), swapping between the two coins using the constant product formula (x * y = k), and a fee mechanism (e.g. 0.3% swap fee). Don't write tests yet
expected_output: A complete Move package with Move.toml and at least one module implementing: Pool struct (shared object), LP token (via Coin), add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, and swap functions. Code should compile with `sui move build` and follow Move idioms.
expectations: Move.toml does not list Sui or MoveStdlib as explicit dependencies (they are implicit in Sui 1.45+) (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#implicit-framework-dependency)
Module declaration uses single-line syntax without curly braces (e.g. `module pkg::amm;`) (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#using-module-label)
Does not use `public entry` — functions are either `public` or `entry` but not both (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#using-module-label)

add_liquidity and remove_liquidity follow pure function pattern (return values to caller, not transfer to sender internally — burns to @0x0 for minimum liquidity locking are acceptable) (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#write-composable-functions-for-ptbs)
Events should be named in past tense (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#events-should-be-named-in-past-tense)
Error constants use EPascalCase naming (e.g. EInsufficientLiquidity) (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#error-constants-are-in-epascalcase)
Function parameters are in the correct order (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#objects-go-first-except-for-clock)
Does not use legacy Coin operations (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#objects-go-first-except-for-clock)
Doc comments start with `///` and logic comments start with `//` (https://move-book.com/guides/code-quality-checklist#comments)
Code compiles successfully with sui move build — no type errors or resource-linearity violations
